newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese army, U.N. sappers detonate bombs.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese army, U.N. sappers detonate bombs.

text.p: Lebanese army and U.N. sappers harmlessly detonated on Saturday four explosive charges planted near a road in a Hizbollah-controlled area of south Lebanon, security sources said.

A Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman in Beirut confirmed the report, saying the explosive charges were discovered between the villages of Derdghayyah and Hmairi east of the port of Tyre, 76 km (48 miles) south of Beirut.

The sources said the charges were found near an area where a local Hizbollah official was killed in an Israeli helicopter ambush in February 1995. Derdghayyah and Hmairi are about 12 km (eight miles) north of Israel's occupation zone in the south.
"The Islamic Resistance informed the security organs and the explosive charges were detonated," the spokesman said.
The sources said army sappers and peacekeepers of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) harmlessly blew up the four charges, planted about 10 metres (yards) apart.
The Islamic Resistance is the military wing of the pro-Iranian fundamantalist group leading a guerrilla war to oust Israeli occupation forces from south Lebanon.
